name: HivePunk 547
subject: pollen-robotics/microduck_rl
thesis: microduck_rl looks like an actively maintained, credible training stack for a small bipedal robot, with recent development focused on walking and recovery policies. Its main uncertainty is real-world validation on shipped hardware, not the existence of the simulation and export workflow.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: pollen-robotics/microduck_rl has 9 raw commits in the last 30 days, 5 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c4cf4da, on 2026-11-10.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: microduck_rl is RL training environments for Microduck, a ~800 g, ~25 cm tall bipedal robot, built on mjlab (MuJoCo Warp) with PPO.
claims.quote: Microduck RL RL training environments for Microduck — a ~800 g, ~25 cm tall bipedal robot — built on mjlab (MuJoCo Warp) with PPO.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Policies are trained at 50 Hz, exported to ONNX, and deployed on the real robot by the runtime in pollen-robotics/microduck.
claims.quote: Policies are trained here at 50 Hz, exported to ONNX, and deployed on the real robot by the runtime in pollen-robotics/microduck .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The repo encodes the full sim2real recipe: BAM actuator physics, domain randomization, backlash simulation, and reward-design lessons.
claims.quote: The repo encodes the full sim2real recipe: BAM actuator physics, domain randomization, backlash simulation, and the reward-design lessons that made it work (see AGENTS.md for the distilled playbook).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Quickstart requires a CUDA GPU because training runs through MuJoCo Warp, and also requires uv.
claims.quote: Quickstart Requires a CUDA GPU (training runs through MuJoCo Warp) and uv .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: On ARM boxes such as DGX Spark / GB10 and Jetson, uv sync pulls about 2 GB of CUDA wheels on first run and the default 30 s HTTP timeout can abort mid-download.
claims.quote: On ARM boxes (DGX Spark / GB10, Jetson): uv sync pulls ~2 GB of CUDA wheels on first run and uv's default 30 s HTTP timeout can abort mid-download.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The main task Mjlab-Velocity-{Flat,Rough}-MicroDuck is walking with velocity commands plus head-pose commands.
claims.quote: Mjlab-Velocity-{Flat,Rough}-MicroDuck flat/rough The main task : walking with velocity commands + head-pose commands

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: At deployment the runtime hot-swaps policies behind a shared 61-dimensional observation contract.
claims.quote: At deployment the runtime hot-swaps these policies (walk / recover / trick) behind a shared 61-dimensional observation contract, so any of them can take over the robot at any moment.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The companion microduck repo says its policies are trained in microduck_rl using MuJoCo and PPO, with ONNX export that the runtime loads.
claims.quote: The policies it runs are trained next door, in microduck_rl — MuJoCo and PPO, the sim2real recipe, and the export to ONNX that this repo loads.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: pollen-robotics/microduck_rl has 9 raw commits in the last 30 days, 5 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c4cf4da, on 2026-11-10.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A community list describes the robot as pre-hardware, with pre-orders open, shipping targeted for December 2026, and almost nobody outside Pollen having a physical unit yet.
claims.quote: The robot is pre-hardware: pre-orders are open, shipping is targeted for December 2026, and almost nobody outside Pollen has a physical unit yet.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: The exact code and model licences, and any security review of exported policies, could not be confirmed from the pages read.
claims.missing: The contents of LICENSE, LICENSE-MODELS.md, and any security or policy-validation documentation

risks: Local training requires a CUDA GPU, creating a hardware barrier.
On ARM machines, the first sync can pull about 2 GB of CUDA wheels and may abort due to a short HTTP timeout without the documented setting.
The ecosystem is described as pre-hardware, so deployment claims outside Pollen are less proven on shipped retail units.
Simulation-to-real performance depends on actuator, backlash, and randomization modelling, which the pages do not independently validate.
Model and code licensing is not confirmed from the pages read, despite LICENSE and LICENSE-MODELS.md files being listed.
unknowns: The exact code and model licences, and any security review of exported policies, could not be confirmed from the pages read.: The contents of LICENSE, LICENSE-MODELS.md, and any security or policy-validation documentation
wouldChangeMind: Evidence that latest policies were validated on many shipped retail units would strengthen the thesis.
Evidence of a sim-to-real gap or serious deployment failures would weaken it.
Clear licence terms for code and models would resolve a key open question.
